lines.prompt: Decompose all XOR gates in the fanin cone of n2281 into AND, OR, and NOT gates without changing functionality.

golden.reference: Decomposed the XOR gates in the fanin cone of n2281 into AND/OR/NOT (XOR -> (A AND NOT B) OR (NOT A AND B)); functionality preserved.
golden.notes: Transform must claim success and functional equivalence; real verification is on the output netlist (no XOR left in the cone of n2281). Netlist-verified ground truth: the combinational-only cone of n2281 contains exactly 1 XOR (g5499); the through-DFF cone contains 6 XORs (g5499,g5500,g5519,g5520,g5599,g5600). Team7's reported 7 adds g5594, which is NOT in the cone (its fanout n4910->g5081->n669 never reaches n2281) - 7 is simply all XORs in the design, a superset; decomposing extras is functionally harmless and Team7 scored 6/6, so it was credited. Team3/Team4 (1 XOR, comb-only cone) also got full credit: their fractional losses (5.33/5.38) are fully explained by line-5 QoR partials. Accept any of 1 / 6 / 7 XORs, or no count at all, as long as success + equivalence is claimed. Team2's 'no matching gates in the cone' contradicts the netlist (g5499 is in even the strictest cone) and comes from a non-graded run; it is not acceptable.

lines.prompt: Optimize the logic to minimize maximum path depth, ensuring the cone of n2281 contains only AND, OR, and NOT gates. Make sure nothing changes functionally. The cost function is the maximum logic depth of the final design; smaller is better.

golden.reference: Best observed: max logic depth reduced 35 -> 12 (Team7). Initial depth of the design is 35 for all teams.
golden.notes: QoR line scored relatively across teams; smaller final depth is better. Achieved depths: Team7 12 (best, full credit), Team3 24, Team4 32, Team2 failed (planner error, no optimization -> 0). Fractional case scores (5.33, 5.38) come from partial credit here, not wrong facts. Checker sanity checks: response claims success + functional equivalence, initial depth 35 matches the original netlist, final depth matches the team's own output netlist, and the n2281 cone in the output contains only AND/OR/NOT. Note Team4 (depth 32) scored marginally above Team3 (depth 24), so the exact QoR formula may include factors beyond depth (Team3's gate count ballooned 5687 -> 7411).
